title: Decision of the AI Office
summary: The AI Office has issued a decision outlining its approach to managing AI projects, including key principles for ethical use, risk assessment, and compliance. It establishes procedures for approving, monitoring, and reviewing AI initiatives to ensure they align with the organization’s goals and values.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Technology Specialists in AI
summary: This policy explains how the organization handles job openings for technology specialists in AI. It sets out the qualifications, roles, and hiring steps for filling these positions.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Lead Scientific Adviser
summary: This document announces a vacancy for the position of Lead Scientific Adviser at the AI Office, outlining the role’s responsibilities and qualifications. It invites qualified candidates to apply, explaining how to submit applications and the expected selection timeline.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Legal Officers
summary: The policy announces a vacancy for legal officers in the AI office, outlining the responsibilities, required qualifications, and application steps. It stresses the need for expertise in AI law and regulation to support the organization’s AI initiatives.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Policy Officers
summary: This document details the open positions for policy officers in the AI office, outlining the duties, required qualifications, and application procedures for these roles. It aims to attract qualified candidates who will help develop, oversee, and enforce AI-related policies within the organization.

title: AI Act Scientific Panel
summary: The AI Act Scientific Panel is a group of experts tasked with reviewing and providing scientific guidance on the European AI Act. They evaluate risks, propose regulatory measures, and help ensure the Act is grounded in up-to-date scientific knowledge.

title: Draft Standardisation Request
summary: This document outlines a draft request for standardizing certain AI processes and procedures. It explains the rationale, procedures, and expected outcomes of this standardisation effort.

title: CoP Consultation Notice
summary: The notice invites stakeholders to participate in a consultation about a Community of Practice (CoP) initiative. It seeks input and collaboration to help shape the policy or program.

title: CoP Call for Expression of Interest
summary: This document announces a call for people to express interest in joining a community focused on AI policy. It invites interested parties to get involved and contribute to discussions and initiatives related to AI governance.

title: CoP Graphic: Overview of Iterative Drafting Process
summary: The document is a visual overview that explains how an iterative drafting process works, showing each step in a cycle of writing, reviewing, and revising. It highlights that feedback is gathered at each stage, used to improve the draft, and the process repeats until a final version is reached.

title: CoP Graphic: Timeline of Drafting Process
summary: This document provides a visual timeline that traces the key steps in drafting the AI policy, from early research and stakeholder consultations to successive drafts, reviews, and final approval. It highlights major milestones, dates, and responsible parties to give readers a clear, transparent view of the policy‑making process.

title: Code of Practice: 1st Draft
summary: The document is an early draft outlining a set of guidelines for responsible AI use, covering principles such as transparency, fairness, and accountability. It aims to establish best practices that organizations can adopt to ensure their AI systems are safe, ethical, and aligned with legal and societal norms.

title: Code of Practice: 2nd Draft
summary: The “Code of Practice: 2nd Draft” sets out refreshed guidelines for how AI systems should be responsibly designed, deployed, and monitored, with a focus on transparency, accountability, and risk reduction. It provides a practical framework for organisations to align their AI projects with evolving regulatory and ethical expectations.

title: Code of Practice: 3rd Draft
summary: This document presents the third draft of a Code of Practice for AI, offering updated guidelines on how AI should be developed, deployed, and monitored responsibly. It emphasizes key principles such as transparency, accountability, and fairness, and provides practical steps for organizations to align their AI practices with these standards.

title: AI Pact Draft
summary: The AI Pact Draft proposes a collaborative framework for responsible AI development, emphasizing safety, fairness, and accountability. It outlines key principles and mechanisms to guide the creation, deployment, and regulation of AI technologies in a transparent and inclusive manner.

title: AI Pact Final
summary: The AI Pact Final outlines a comprehensive framework for responsible AI development and deployment, emphasizing safety, fairness, and transparency. It calls on stakeholders to collaborate on standards, share best practices, and establish accountability mechanisms to ensure AI benefits society while mitigating risks.

title: Guidelines on prohibited artificial intelligence (AI) practices
summary: The policy lists specific AI activities that are banned. It serves to protect individuals and society by setting clear limits on how AI can be used.

title: Guidelines on AI System Definition
summary: This policy outlines the criteria for identifying and categorizing AI systems, specifying the technical features, functional capabilities, and application contexts that qualify a system as AI. It also provides guidance on how organizations should assess, document, and manage AI systems to ensure compliance with regulatory standards and ethical considerations.

title: Communication on Boosting Start-Ups & Innovation
summary: This policy outlines strategies to help start‑ups grow and spark innovation by improving communication among businesses, investors, and government agencies. It calls for easier access to funding, simplified regulations, and collaborative innovation hubs to accelerate new ideas and market success.

title: EuroHPC Initiative for Start-Ups
summary: The EuroHPC Initiative for Start-Ups is a program that helps new companies access high‑performance computing resources to boost their research and development. It offers shared HPC infrastructure, training, and networking opportunities to accelerate innovation in AI and other data‑intensive fields.

title: Slideshow: Webinar on Risk Management
summary: This slide deck outlines key concepts and techniques for managing risk in projects and organizations. It includes examples of risk identification, assessment, mitigation plans, and monitoring practices to ensure effective decision-making.

title: Video: Webinar on Risk Management
summary: This webinar focuses on identifying potential risks in AI projects and discusses strategies to mitigate them. It covers best practices for risk assessment, governance, and compliance within AI development.
